acceptance_criteria: AC-1: compile_failover_plan never performs I/O -- proven by the poison session_resolver over every fixture, including a SAFE_TO_FAILOVER unit.

AC-2: plan_compilable is False with a named compilation_blocked_reason for unresolved cluster mode, non-HA cluster mode, ambiguous/missing member roles, and every non-ClusterXL unit type; never a fabricated plan.
AC-3: FailoverPlan.step.preconditions carries exactly the seven STOP_CONDITIONS verbatim from compute_ha_readiness for every plan_compilable=True case -- generated matrix test.
AC-4: ReversalStep.intended_postcondition reproduces build_plan()'s existing three-way D-V7b disclosure unchanged; a regression test proves no fourth value is ever invented.
AC-5: DryRunReport.would_proceed is True iff plan_compilable and readiness_verdict == SAFE_TO_FAILOVER -- exhaustive over the verdict enum.
AC-6: CLASS_2_OPERATIONAL_STATE_CHANGE gains no member; DenyAllAuthorizer remains the only production Authorizer -- regression test.
AC-7: architecture-convergence test asserts no module under utils/operate/ or checkpoint/clusterxl_capability_adapter.py imports utils.failover_plan.
AC-8: --failover-plan-dry-run performs no network/credential access -- CLI smoke test over a fixture unified.json, matching --ha-readiness-check's existing test pattern.

baseline.authority: docs/history/phase/OP_1_FAILOVER_PLAN_COMPILER_AND_DRY_RUN.md (FROZEN -- PRODUCT OWNER APPROVED 2026-09-09) is the complete implementation authority: section 3 (FailoverPlan schema), section 4 (compilation from CPClusterXLCapabilityAdapter's two pure methods with the poison session_resolver), section 5 (DryRunReport), section 6 (structural separation from utils/operate), section 7 (vendor scope: classic ClusterXL only, everything else compilation_blocked_reason), section 9 (the slice: 5 non-test files, 8 acceptance criteria). Read it in full before writing code; do not re-derive anything it already decides.
baseline.sequencing: Independent of every in-flight movement. Does NOT wait for the real-hardware OP.0 readiness campaign: the compiler consumes compute_ha_readiness / OP.0b preflight evidence the platform already stores and runs no command. A real-environment validation of a compiled plan is a later, separate, Product-Owner-run step.

context_not_loaded: Any device contact, credential, or network access -- this slice is offline by construction
Option B of op_degraded_verdict (risk_items, severity fields, reopening utils/failover/assessment.py::_verdict_for) -- rejected at freeze, out of scope
Any Operator Console job type, Palo Alto HA, or VSX/VSLS support -- section 9 'deliberately not in this slice'
invariants: compile_failover_plan performs no I/O -- it is constructed with a poison session_resolver that raises if ever invoked, and every test asserts it is never invoked

The new package is utils/failover_plan/ -- NOT utils/failover/ and NOT utils/operate/; both of those packages have test-enforced exact module allowlists that exist precisely to keep a plan/executor out (section 9 files item 1). Do not touch either allowlist.

utils.action_taxonomy.CLASS_2_OPERATIONAL_STATE_CHANGE gains no member; DenyAllAuthorizer remains the only production Authorizer (AC-6). Nothing in this slice may construct ActionCoordinator or call check_precondition()/execute_once()/observe_postcondition()
One-way dependency: nothing under utils/operate/ or checkpoint/clusterxl_capability_adapter.py may import utils.failover_plan (AC-7)
readiness_verdict can only ever be SAFE_TO_FAILOVER / UNSAFE_DO_NOT_FAILOVER / INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE / NOT_A_FAILOVER_UNIT -- Option A; never invent a reachable DEGRADED path
Never fabricate a plan: unresolved/non-HA cluster mode, ambiguous member roles, or any non-ClusterXL unit type yields plan_compilable=False with a named compilation_blocked_reason (AC-2)

Deliver the write-free failover plan compiler, its dry-run evaluator, and one offline CLI mode, for classic Check Point ClusterXL only.
